official_code_source.publisher: Office of the Law Revision Counsel, U.S. House of Representatives
official_code_source.title: 26 U.S.C. §1, Tax imposed, preliminary edition
structural_findings: section 1(j)(2)(A) through (D) contain the four individual filing-status rate tables
section 1(j)(2)(E) separately governs estates and trusts

draft_identity.short_title: Taxlane Ordinary Individual Rate Schedule Discussion Draft

amendment_mechanic.method: direct the Secretary, for the individual tables prescribed under section 1(j)(3)(B), to substitute the seven specified ordinary rates while preserving every bracket threshold and indexing rule
does_not_apply_to: any tax parameter outside the express ordinary individual rate substitutions

administrative_directions: Treasury must revise wage and pension withholding methods as soon as practicable.
Previously published 2026 withholding methods remain usable until the mandatory date in implementing guidance.
Reasonable-cause and estimated-tax relief applies when an underpayment is attributable solely to pre-guidance use of the prior schedule.
Treasury must update forms, instructions, e-file schemas, and other implementation materials.
Nothing in the draft supplies or deems an appropriation.
conformance_questions_for_legislative_co: Whether a new section 1(j)(7) or replacement tables in section 1(j)(2)(A) through (D) are the preferred drafting form.
Whether additional cross-references to section 1(c) rates require conforming amendments beyond section 1(j)(2)(F).
Whether the section 15 nonapplication clause is necessary for a taxable-year effective date enacted after January 1, 2026.
Whether withholding and estimated-tax transition relief belongs in statutory text or Treasury guidance.
Whether any budget-act, PAYGO, or administrative-appropriation language is required for an introduced measure.
public_warning: This is a nonofficial discussion draft prepared to make Legislative Counsel review easier. It is not Legislative Counsel text, an introduced bill, an official proposal, enacted law, an official score, or a certified rate or balance determination.
